title: Leaflet cluster map of talk locations
text:
Assuming you are working in a Linux or Windows Subsystem for Linux environment, you may need to install some dependencies. Assuming a clean installation, the following will be needed:
sudo apt install jupyter
sudo apt install python3-pip
pip install python-frontmatter getorg --upgrade
After which you can run this from the _talks/ directory, via:
 jupyter nbconvert --to notebook --execute talkmap.ipynb --output talkmap_out.ipynb
The _talks/ directory contains .md files of all your talks. This scrapes the location YAML field from each .md file, geolocates it with geopy/Nominatim, and uses the getorg library to output data, HTML, and Javascript for a standalone cluster map.

In the event that this times out with an error, double check to make sure that the location is can be properly geolocated.

# Perform geolocation
for file in g:
    # Read the file
    data = frontmatter.load(file)
    data = data.to_dict()

    # Press on if the location is not present
    if 'location' not in data:
        continue

    # Prepare the description
    title = data['title'].strip()
    venue = data['venue'].strip()
    location = data['location'].strip()
    description = f"{title}<br />{venue}; {location}"

    # Geocode the location and report the status
    try:
        location_dict[description] = geocoder.geocode(location, timeout=TIMEOUT)
        print(description, location_dict[description])
    except ValueError as ex:
        print(f"Error: geocode failed on input {location} with message {ex}")
    except GeocoderTimedOut as ex:
        print(f"Error: geocode timed out on input {location} with message {ex}")
    except Exception as ex:
        print(f"An unhandled exception occurred while processing input {location} with message {ex}")

title: Roy Plant–Microbiome Lab
text:
orcid = '0000-0000-0000-0000' # Fill your orcid here


import requests

We use the /works api to list all works related to the orcid. This gives a summary of all works, so citation information is not included. We collect the put-code of all works to retrieve the citation information later.

response = requests.get('https://pub.orcid.org/v3.0/{}/works'.format(orcid),
                        headers={"Accept": "application/orcid+json" })
record = response.json()


put_codes = []
for work in record['group']:
    put_code = work['work-summary'][0]['put-code']
    put_codes.append(put_code)
put_code = put_codes[0]

We use the /<orcid>/work/<put-code> endpoint to retrieve the citation information for each record.

citations = []
for put_code in put_codes:
    response = requests.get('https://pub.orcid.org/v3.0/{}/work/{}'.format(orcid, put_code),
                            headers={"Accept": "application/orcid+json" })
    work = response.json()
    if work['citation'] is not None:
        citations.append(work['citation']['citation-value'])


with open('output.bib', 'w') as bibfile:
    for citation in citations:
        bibfile.write(citation)
        bibfile.write('\n')

section: Advancing Sustainable Agriculture through Plant–Microbiome Research
text:
Advancing Sustainable Agriculture through Plant–Microbiome Research
Welcome to the Roylawar Plant–Microbiome Research Laboratory, where we explore the fascinating interactions between plants and microorganisms to develop sustainable solutions for agriculture. Our research integrates microbiology, molecular biology, ecology, bioinformatics, and biotechnology to improve crop productivity and resilience.

title: Home
text:
Research Focus


🌱 Rhizosphere Microbiome
Understanding the diversity and function of microbial communities associated with plant roots.


🧬 Plant–Microbe Interactions
Investigating beneficial microbial interactions to improve crop productivity and resilience.


🧅 Wild Allium Biology
Exploring wild Allium species as valuable genetic and microbiome resources.


🦠 Metagenomics & Microbial Ecology
Applying next-generation sequencing to characterize complex microbial communities.


🧪 Synthetic Microbial Communities
Designing SynComs for sustainable crop production and disease management.


🌾 Climate-Resilient Agriculture
Developing microbiome-based strategies for sustainable and climate-resilient farming.

title: Contributing Guide
text:
Contributing Guide
Thank you for contributing to the Roy Plant–Microbiome Laboratory website.
This document describes the workflow for updating and maintaining the website.



Website Technology
This website is built using:

Quarto
HTML
CSS
Git
GitHub Pages

Source files are written in .qmd format and rendered into the docs/ directory.



Project Structure
ThePlant-Roylawar.github.io

│
├── index.qmd
├── about.qmd
├── research.qmd
├── projects.qmd
├── team.qmd
├── publications.qmd
├── news.qmd
├── join.qmd
├── contact.qmd
│
├── styles.css
├── footer.html
├── images/
├── docs/
│
├── CHANGELOG.md
├── PROJECT_STATUS.md
├── WEBSITE_ROADMAP.md
├── DEVELOPMENT_LOG.md
└── CONTRIBUTING.md



Development Workflow
Every change should follow the same workflow.

1. Edit files
Modify only the required files.
Example:

index.qmd
research.qmd
styles.css




2. Render the website
quarto render



3. Review
Open the local website and verify:

Desktop layout
Mobile layout
Images
Links
Typography




4. Git Status
git status
Review the modified files before committing.



5. Stage Changes
git add .



6. Commit
Use meaningful commit messages.
Examples:
git commit -m "Homepage v2.2: Add Latest News section"
git commit -m "Research page: Improve project cards"



7. Push
git push




Website Design Principles
The website should:

Maintain a clean academic appearance.
Use original laboratory images whenever possible.
Prioritize readability.
Follow responsive design.
Keep a consistent green colour palette.
Avoid unnecessary visual clutter.
Maintain consistent spacing across all pages.




Editing Rules
Before making changes:

Work on one feature at a time.
Render after every major change.
Review visually before committing.
Avoid editing multiple unrelated sections in one commit.




Homepage Structure
The homepage follows this fixed structure.

Hero
About the Lab
Research Impact
Featured Research
Research Collaborations
Latest News
Join the Lab
Footer

This structure should remain consistent unless there is a compelling reason for a future redesign.



Documentation
Whenever a milestone is completed, update:

CHANGELOG.md
PROJECT_STATUS.md

If the project direction changes significantly, update:

WEBSITE_ROADMAP.md
DEVELOPMENT_LOG.md




Branch Strategy
Development currently occurs on the master branch.
Future improvements may use feature branches before merging into the main website.

Our interdisciplinary research combines microbiology, plant pathology, metagenomics, nanotechnology, molecular biology, and bioinformatics to develop innovative solutions for sustainable agriculture, crop health, and environmental resilience.

title: News
text: Welcome to the latest news from the Roylawar Plant–Microbiome Research Laboratory. Here we share research achievements, student accomplishments, publications, collaborations, internships, and other important laboratory milestones.

title: News
text:
📄 Publication Alert
We are delighted to share our recent publication:
“Microbial allies in a cotton pest: A descriptive account of associated microbiota dynamics in Dysdercus cingulatus across development”
published in Comparative Biochemistry and Physiology Part D: Genomics and Proteomics.
The study began with a scientific question aimed at understanding the microbial communities associated with the cotton pest Dysdercus cingulatus. Through experimental design, sequencing, microbiome analysis, data interpretation, and manuscript preparation, the project evolved into a valuable scientific contribution.
Congratulations to Ms. Pravara Rupawate for her dedication, scientific curiosity, and perseverance throughout the project.
Special congratulations to Dr. Seema Borgave for her continuous guidance, mentorship, and unwavering support in transforming this research idea into a published scientific contribution.

title: News
section: 🇫🇮 Successful Completion of Ph.D. Research Visit
text:
🇫🇮 Successful Completion of Ph.D. Research Visit
Ms. Shreya Kasar successfully completed her six-month Ph.D. research visit to the Department of Microbiology, University of Helsinki, Finland.
During her visit, she received advanced training in:

Metagenomic data analysis
Functional microbiome analysis
Bioinformatics

The visit resulted in:

Advanced expertise in microbiome bioinformatics
Strengthened international research collaborations
Significant progress toward her doctoral research
Long-term collaborative opportunities between the collaborating institutions

title: News
section: 🏆 Ph.D. Scholar Upgraded to Senior Research Fellow
text:
🏆 Ph.D. Scholar Upgraded to Senior Research Fellow
Congratulations to Ms. Avantika Jakati on her successful upgradation to the position of Senior Research Fellow (SRF).
This achievement recognizes her excellent research progress and continued contribution to her doctoral research on plastic-degrading bacteria and antibiotic resistance in wastewater treatment sludge.

title: News
section: 🌱 Eight Students Join ICAR-DOGR Internship Programme
text:
🌱 Eight Students Join ICAR-DOGR Internship Programme
As the MoU Coordinator between our institution and ICAR – Directorate of Onion and Garlic Research (ICAR-DOGR), I am pleased to share that eight students from the Department of Botany have joined the three-month internship programme at ICAR-DOGR.
The internship provides students with valuable hands-on training in modern agricultural research, laboratory techniques, and onion and garlic research.

title: News
text:
🎉 NGSF Fellowship Award
Congratulations to Ms. Lina Sonawane on being selected for the NGSF Fellowship to undertake a three-month internship programme at ICAR – Directorate of Onion and Garlic Research (ICAR-DOGR).
We wish her every success in her research journey.

title: News
section: 🎓 Prestigious EDUFI Fellowship & International Research Achievement
text:
🎓 Prestigious EDUFI Fellowship & International Research Achievement
I am delighted to share a milestone that reflects the value of mentorship, collaboration, and perseverance.
My first Ph.D. student, Ms. Shreya Kasar, was awarded the prestigious EDUFI Fellowship by the Finnish National Agency for Education, enabling her to undertake a fully funded six-month research visit to the Department of Microbiology, University of Helsinki, Finland.
Through this fellowship, she completed a significant part of her doctoral research while receiving advanced training in metagenomics, functional microbiome analysis, and bioinformatics.
This achievement is particularly significant because:

She is the first Ph.D. student from our college to complete a substantial part of her doctoral research through an international collaboration.
She is the first student from the Department of Botany under Savitribai Phule Pune University (SPPU) to receive the prestigious EDUFI Fellowship.

This accomplishment reflects her dedication, perseverance, and scientific commitment, together with the continuous encouragement and support of our institution and collaborators.

title: Research
text: The Roylawar Plant–Microbiome Research Laboratory investigates the interactions between plants and microorganisms to develop sustainable solutions for agriculture, crop protection, and environmental resilience. Our research integrates molecular biology, microbiology, plant pathology, metagenomics, bioinformatics, and microbial ecology.

title: Research
text:
🌱 Rhizosphere Microbiome
We investigate the diversity, composition, and functional potential of rhizosphere microbial communities associated with cultivated and wild plant species. By integrating next-generation sequencing and bioinformatics, we aim to understand how beneficial microorganisms influence plant growth, nutrient acquisition, and stress tolerance.
Current focus:

Wild Allium species
Microbial diversity analysis
Functional metagenomics
Soil microbial ecology

title: Research
text:
🧬 Plant–Microbe Interactions
Understanding the complex interactions between plants and beneficial microorganisms forms the foundation of our research. We explore mechanisms through which microbes enhance plant health, suppress diseases, and improve productivity under diverse environmental conditions.
Research areas include:

Beneficial bacteria
Beneficial fungi
Root colonization
Plant immune responses

title: Research
text:
🦠 Metagenomics and Bioinformatics
High-throughput sequencing technologies allow us to characterize microbial communities without cultivation. We employ bioinformatics pipelines to investigate microbial diversity, taxonomic composition, functional genes, and ecological interactions.
Current approaches:

16S rRNA sequencing
ITS sequencing
Functional annotation
Microbial network analysis

title: Research
text:
🧪 Synthetic Microbial Communities (SynComs)
One of our long-term objectives is the development of synthetic microbial communities capable of enhancing crop productivity and resilience. We identify beneficial microorganisms and combine them into microbial consortia for sustainable agricultural applications.
Applications include:

Plant growth promotion
Disease suppression
Nutrient mobilization
Climate resilience

title: Research
text:
🌾 Sustainable Agriculture
Our laboratory develops environmentally friendly strategies to reduce dependence on chemical fertilizers and pesticides by utilizing beneficial microorganisms and microbiome engineering.
Major research directions:

Biofertilizers
Biocontrol agents
Soil health
Climate-smart agriculture

title: Research
text:
🧅 Allium Research
A major research focus of our laboratory is the biology and improvement of onion and other Allium species. Our work integrates microbiome research, molecular biology, plant pathology, and stress physiology to improve crop performance and resilience.
Current topics include:

Wild Allium diversity
Onion microbiome
Salinity tolerance
Disease resistance
Root-associated microorganisms
